text: Octopuses can rapidly change both skin color and texture under nervous control, transforming the appearance of a soft body.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, giant Pacific octopus research and exhibit report; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/news/smithsonians-national-zoo-gets-new-giant-pacific-octopus. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Some midwater animals have light organs on their underside. Matching the brightness of water above them can erase the silhouette a predator below would otherwise see.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA Ocean Exploration, Ocean Zones curriculum, section 5; https://oceanexplorer.noaa.gov/edu/curriculum/section5.pdf. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Marine bioluminescence comes from chemical reactions in living organisms. Different species use light to communicate, attract prey, or disrupt a predator's attack.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: NOAA National Ocean Service, bioluminescence; https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/biolum.html. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Monarch caterpillars feed on milkweed. A butterfly species can depend on particular host plants during its larval stage.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, North Coast and Cascades butterfly inventory; nomenclature follows the cited inventory; https://www.nps.gov/articles/butterflies-of-the-north-coast-and-cascades.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Pine white butterfly larvae use conifer needles, including those of pines, Douglas-fir, and true firs.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, North Coast and Cascades butterfly inventory; nomenclature follows the cited inventory; https://www.nps.gov/articles/butterflies-of-the-north-coast-and-cascades.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
